description:
FILED s530c (Opus agent, 2026-10-31) as the residue of #3864 -- a PPI LEXING question, so CITED for the PPI-at-source program (docs/ppi-fix-at-source-s527.md), not taken.  PRE-EXISTING.

#3864 makes `${name{KEY}}` / `${name[IDX]}` / `@{name[LIST]}` the element / slice (Pl::PExpr::_block_word_subscript).  When NAME is a quote-like operator word (m q qq qw qr qx s y tr), PPI does not build Word + Block: it lexes `m{q}` as a Regexp::Match token (`s{x}`, `y[1]` likewise), so the deref block holds ONE quote-like token and the collapse cannot see a name:

    sub g { my %m = (q => 'r'); return ${m{q}} } print g(), "\n";
  perl 5.40.3: r        PCL (s530c): (empty -- a match of /q/ against $_)
Probe scratch/s530c/pr/br2.pl row 13.

toke.c S_scan_ident reads an IDENTIFIER right after `${` (and `@{`) before any operator lookup, so inside `${ ... }` a leading `m` / `s` / `y` / `q...` followed by an opening bracket is the variable name.  PPI's tokenizer has no such state for the inside of a `${` block.  Fix belongs on the `pcl` branch of vendor/PPI (Token::Cast / the Word lexer after `${`); once it lexes Word + Block, #3864's collapse takes the shape with no further PCL change.


ADDENDUM (s530c, same session): a second spelling of the same family, LOUD rather than silent -- `${sub[0]}` (perl: @sub's element; toke.c excludes the name `sub` only for the `{` spelling).  PPI builds Word `sub` + Constructor, #3864's collapse produces `$sub` + subscript, yet the statement is DROPPED ("Handle single node of unknown type") -- something upstream of the collapse reads the `sub` Word as an anonymous sub.  The base (ff265320) dies on it too.  Probe scratch/s530c/pr/br4.pl row c.  Rare; recorded here with its sibling rather than as its own task.
subject: PPI lexes `${m{q}}` / `${s{x}}` / `${y[1]}` (a quote-like word as the NAME of a braced element) as a regex / transliteration, so #3864's element collapse cannot see it -- silent wrong; a PPI lexing fix (cited for the PPI program)
